checkpoints: Multer enforces `limits.fileSize` by aborting the multipart stream mid-transfer the moment the byte count crosses the configured cap, and it does this while `FileInterceptor` is still parsing the request body — before the route handler ever executes.

Because the abort happens inside the interceptor layer, the route handler's own logic (including any `if (!file)` check written for the wrong-MIME case) never runs for an oversized upload, so a try/catch placed inside the handler cannot intercept this failure.

When the size limit trips, Multer throws its own error class, `MulterError`, with `code = "LIMIT_FILE_SIZE"` — this is not a NestJS `HttpException`, so it carries no built-in mapping to an HTTP status.

NestJS's default exception handling only knows how to translate `HttpException` instances into structured responses; an unrecognized error type like `MulterError` falls through that default handling and surfaces as a generic 500 with a raw stack trace instead of a meaningful status.

The fix is a dedicated exception filter — a class implementing `ExceptionFilter` decorated with `@Catch(MulterError)` — that switches on `exception.code`, mapping `LIMIT_FILE_SIZE` to a 413 Payload Too Large response and other Multer error codes to 400, each with a standardized JSON body.

Registering the filter globally via `app.useGlobalFilters(...)` in `main.ts`, rather than scoping it to one controller with `@UseFilters`, ensures every upload route in the application gets covered by the same mapping instead of only the endpoint being debugged.

Returning 413 instead of 500 changes what the response communicates to the client: 413 signals a client-side problem (the file itself was too large) so the client can show a targeted message and avoid retrying, whereas 500 implies a server fault and exposes internal error detail with no actionable next step.

Fixing this correctly means verifying an over-limit upload now returns 413 with the standardized body while a valid-size upload still returns 201 and a wrong-MIME upload still returns 415 — proving the new filter only intercepts `MulterError` and leaves the controller's own MIME-check path untouched.
